title: The Palace Model
lead: Method-of-loci + Zettelkasten mapped onto concrete data structures.
summary: The Palace Model is MemPalace's spatial memory architecture: Wings (people/projects) contain Rooms (days/topics), which hold Drawers (verbatim text ~800 chars). Hallways connect entities within wings; Tunnels link rooms across wings. The index layer (Closets) stores compact topic/entity/quote pointers that lead searchers to drawers. Dating metadata (Tier 6a) and Diaries bring temporal scoping. Dynamics (Hebbian strength + Ebbinghaus decay) make connections fade or strengthen based on use and spacing.

concepts.definition: A named broad category (person, project, department) derived from a directory name. Normalized to lowercase with underscores replacing hyphens and spaces. Drawers tagged with a wing can be filtered, scoped, or tracked as a unit.
A time-based or topic-based grouping within a wing, e.g. 'diary', 'meetings', 'design-docs'. Detected from file paths, filenames, or keywords during mining. Rooms span multiple wings via Tunnels.

A chunk of verbatim source text (~800 chars), immutable once written. Identified by drawer_ID = drawer_WING_ROOM_SHA256-hash(source-file+chunk-index). Stores original content, entities, halls, dates, and line numbers.

A searchable index record (in mempalace_closets collection) containing compact topic/entity/quote pointer lines that reference one or more drawers. Built during mining by extract→pointer→pack logic; packed greedily up to 1,500 chars per closet.

A within-wing connector materializing entity-pair co-occurrence. If entities Aya and Lumi appear together in 2+ drawers in the same wing, a hallway records the pair, count, and rooms where they co-occurred. Persisted in hallways.json.

A cross-wing link between two rooms (or synthetic topic:/entity: rooms). Explicit tunnels are user-created; topic and entity tunnels auto-generate when shared topics or entities are detected across wings. Persisted in tunnels.json.

A dated journal entry or conversation log mined from a transcript file. The timestamp (ISO YYYY-MM-DD) is extracted from the filename, frontmatter, content, or mtime and stored as content_date in drawer metadata, enabling temporal grouping.

Living-connection math: Hebbian potentiation (strength grows on co-access), Ebbinghaus decay (fades over time), Cepeda spacing effect (stability grows on spaced reinforcement). Applied identically to hallways and tunnels to rank by salience.

symbols.name: add_drawer
symbols.role: Core API to add one drawer to the collection with deterministic ID derivation and metadata tagging.

symbols.name: build_closet_lines
symbols.role: Extract topics, entities, and quotes from drawer content into atomic pointer lines for the closet index.

symbols.name: upsert_closet_lines
symbols.role: Pack pointer lines greedily into closets respecting CLOSET_CHAR_LIMIT, write atomically, return count.

symbols.name: compute_hallways_for_wing
symbols.role: Scan a wing's drawers, count entity-pair co-occurrence (min 2), create hallway records with preserved dynamics.

symbols.name: create_tunnel
symbols.role: Create explicit or auto-generated tunnels with symmetric deduplication, validate room existence, persist with dynamics.

symbols.name: build_graph
symbols.role: Traverse drawers, build in-memory room nodes and cross-wing edges, return cached result within TTL.

symbols.name: potentiate
symbols.role: Strengthen connection on co-access event; grow stability only if spaced >1 hour; cap strength at MAX_STRENGTH.

symbols.name: apply_decay
symbols.role: Apply Ebbinghaus exponential decay to connection strength based on time since last activation and stability.

symbols.name: normalize_wing_name
symbols.role: Canonical wing slug: lowercase, replace hyphens and spaces with underscores. Used at write and read boundaries.

symbols.name: CLOSET_CHAR_LIMIT
symbols.role: Max chars per closet document (1,500) before opening a new numbered closet.

symbols.name: _hallway_id
symbols.role: Deterministic hallway ID from wing and sorted entity pair, enabling symmetric deduplication.

symbols.name: _canonical_tunnel_id
symbols.role: Symmetric tunnel ID from sorted wing/room endpoints, enabling dedup across call order.

surprises.title: Drawers Are Immutable; Metadata Is Updated In-Place
surprises.detail: Once a drawer's content is written, it never changes. Re-mining a file deletes the old drawers for that source_file and writes new ones. But the drawer's document text is append-only by design. The metadata (entities, hall, content_date) can be updated on upsert, but the verbatim content block is frozen. This matches the 'Incremental only' principle: never destroy data to rebuild.

surprises.title: Closets Are Not Stored as Individual Records; They're Batched
surprises.detail: Each Closet ID (e.g., closet_base_01, closet_base_02) is a single upsert covering multiple pointer lines, packed greedily. They're not one pointer line per closet; rather, pointer lines are batched into closets up to the char limit. This packing is deterministic — the same source file produces the same closet numbering.

surprises.title: Dynamics Are Preserved Across Re-Mines to Prevent Reset
surprises.detail: When a hallway or tunnel is recomputed (e.g., on a fresh mine of the wing), the code explicitly copies over the prior record's strength, stability, last_activated, and access_count before initializing any missing fields. Without this preservation, every mine would reset the connection weights to defaults, wiping accumulated salience. This is a subtle but critical detail for the living-connection layer.

surprises.title: Topic and Entity Tunnels Use Synthetic Room Prefixes
surprises.detail: Auto-generated topic and entity tunnels don't link literal rooms; they use synthetic room identifiers: topic:Angular, entity:Ben. This namespaces them away from folder-derived rooms so a wing with a literal 'Angular' folder room remains distinct from a 'Angular' topic tunnel. The prefix is also visible to LLMs scanning the tunnel list, making the distinction machine-readable.

surprises.title: Tier 6a Date+Line Segment Is Backward Compatible
surprises.detail: Closet pointers have two formats: legacy 3-segment (topic|entities|→drawer_ids) and Tier 6a 4-segment (topic|entities|YYYY-MM-DD:Lstart-Lend|→drawer_ids). The builder tries to emit the 4-segment form when line_start/line_end and filed_at (or content_date) are available, but falls back to 3-segment if any field is missing. This allows closet pointers from pre-Tier-6a drawers and direct callers without metadata to coexist with modern pointers in the same collection.

designDecisions.decision: Drawers are content chunks, not whole files; closets are the index.
designDecisions.rationale: Splitting content into ~800-char drawers avoids embedding the entire file and allows fine-grained retrieval. Closets (the index layer) point to drawers, enabling search to hit the closet first (fast, small documents) and only fetch the drawers needed. This two-layer design matches the Zettelkasten principle: small index cards (closets) that point to larger content (drawers).

designDecisions.decision: Wing names are normalized at the boundary; queries compare normalized forms.
designDecisions.rationale: Normalizing wing names (lowercasing, collapsing separators) at write-time and reading time ensures that mempalace-public and mempalace_public resolve to the same wing. This handles the mismatch between directory names (which may use hyphens) and YAML slugs (which may use underscores), keeping the palace consistent while allowing flexible user input.

designDecisions.decision: Topic and entity tunnels use synthetic room prefixes (topic:, entity:).
designDecisions.rationale: Auto-generated tunnels shouldn't collide with literal folder-derived rooms. By prefixing synthetic room identifiers, the code keeps the graph clean and makes it easy for readers (including LLMs) to distinguish real-room traversals from topical links. This also avoids hidden collisions when a wing has both a literal 'Angular' folder and a shared 'Angular' topic.

designDecisions.decision: Hallways and tunnels preserve dynamics fields across re-mines.
designDecisions.rationale: Accumulated salience (strength, stability, access_count) represents the lived history of a connection. Resetting them on every mine would defeat the living-connection layer. By preserving these fields and re-initializing only missing ones, the palace maintains a durable memory of which connections matter most based on actual use patterns.

designDecisions.decision: Closets are built greedily, not bin-packed; lines are never split.
designDecisions.rationale: Greedy packing is simpler to implement and reason about than optimal bin-packing, while still achieving compact storage. Atomic lines (never split across closets) mean each pointer is self-contained and searchable, reducing the chance of partial matches and keeping the index format clean.

related.why: The Palace Model is the core spatial structure described in the system architecture; this page details how the model is implemented.
Closets and their pointer-line format connect to AAAK compression, the symbolic dialect that lets LLMs scan the index efficiently.
The temporal knowledge graph stores entity relationships and dates, complementing the spatial palace structure with temporal and semantic edges.
Search uses closets as the primary index and falls back to drawer search; the retrieval layer depends on the palace model's structure.
Project mining creates drawers, rooms, wings, and entities, populating the palace model with content.
Conversation mining also creates drawers and diarized rooms, bringing transcripts into the palace with temporal dating.

searchDoc.title: The Palace Model
searchDoc.summary: MemPalace's spatial memory architecture: wings contain rooms, which hold immutable verbatim drawers; closets index them; hallways and tunnels connect entities and wings; dynamics make connections fade or strengthen by use.
searchDoc.body: The Palace Model is MemPalace's spatial memory architecture, mapping the method of loci and the Zettelkasten onto concrete data structures. A palace is organized as a tree. Wings are named broad categories derived from directory names, normalized to lowercase with underscores replacing hyphens and spaces. Rooms are time- or topic-based groupings within a wing, detected from file paths, filenames, or keywords during mining. Drawers are immutable chunks of verbatim source text of about 800 characters, identified by a deterministic SHA256 hash of the source file path plus chunk index, wrapped as drawer_WING_ROOM_hexsuffix. Each drawer stores original content plus metadata: wing, room, source file, chunk index, filed_at ingestion time, a detected hall keyword, entities (capitalized words appearing two or more times), and optionally content_date, line_start, and line_end for precise source location under Tier 6a. Closets are the searchable index layer in the mempalace_closets collection. The builder reads the first 5,000 characters of a drawer and emits atomic pointer lines for topics, double-quoted spans, and entity pairs, then packs them greedily into closet documents up to 1,500 characters without splitting a line. Pointer lines come in legacy three-segment form and Tier 6a four-segment form with an optional date and line span, falling back when fields are missing so old and new pointers coexist. Hallways are within-wing connectors materializing entity-pair co-occurrence: any pair appearing together in two or more drawers gets a hallway record tracking the pair, count, and rooms, persisted in hallways.json with symmetric IDs from the sorted entity pair. Tunnels are cross-wing links in three flavors: explicit user-created links, auto-generated topic tunnels using synthetic topic: room identifiers, and auto-generated entity tunnels using entity: identifiers, all stored in tunnels.json and deduplicated by canonical sorted-endpoint ID. Dynamics give both hallways and tunnels a living-connection layer with four fields: strength as a Hebbian weight between 0.05 and 5.0, stability as decay resistance, last_activated, and access_count. Hebbian potentiation grows strength on co-access; Ebbinghaus exponential decay fades it over time floored at 0.05; and the Cepeda spacing effect grows stability only when reinforcement is spaced more than an hour apart. Critically, dynamics fields are preserved across re-mines so accumulated salience never resets. On search, queries hit closets first, parse out drawer IDs, fetch those drawers, and rank by distance, falling back to direct drawer search. The palace_graph module builds a cached in-memory graph from drawer metadata with a 60-second TTL invalidated on writes.
